bibl.title: Navigating from hippocampus to parietal cortex
bibl.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: how allocentric spatial maps in entorhinal cortex and hippocampus are converted into body-centred signals that can guide movement
span.quote: To traverse the environment, animals must be able to translate coordinate information from spatial maps in the entorhinal cortex and hippocampus into body-centered representations that can be used to direct locomotion. How this is done remains an enigma.

span.label: which structure performs the transformation from map coordinates to egocentric motor output
span.quote: However, the entorhinal-hippocampal circuit alone cannot be sufficient for implementing the full array of computations necessary for spatial behavior. In addition to possessing a universal map of space, animals must also be able to convert the spatial information into goal-oriented motor output.

span.label: proposes posterior parietal cortex as the site of that transformation, and assembles the primate and rodent evidence for it
span.quote: We propose here that this translation involves a transformation of output from the MEC circuit into body-based coordinates in parietal cortex, and that this transformation, aided by strong connections from parietal cortex to motor and premotor cortex ( 33 , 34 ), is necessary for guiding locomotor output during goal-oriented navigation.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We hypothesize that the essential contribution of the PPC is the translation of the animal's position from a world-centered coordinate system generated by place cells and grid cells into the body-based coordinates of locomotor actions.

span.label: spatial navigation in rodents
span.quote: The navigational system of the mammalian cortex comprises a number of interacting brain regions.

span.label: review
span.quote: A large body of work, involving rats, monkeys, and humans, has consistently supported the conclusion that PPC is essential for key aspects of spatial representation ( 35 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Output of the medial entorhinal grid-cell circuit is transformed into body-based coordinates in parietal cortex, and parietal projections to motor and premotor cortex then convert those coordinates into locomotor commands.
span.quote: We propose here that this translation involves a transformation of output from the MEC circuit into body-based coordinates in parietal cortex, and that this transformation, aided by strong connections from parietal cortex to motor and premotor cortex ( 33 , 34 ), is necessary for guiding locomotor output during goal-oriented navigation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: World-referenced and body-referenced signals converge multiplicatively on single PPC neurons, and this conjunctive (gain-field) coding is what performs the allocentric-to-egocentric conversion.
span.quote: These studies indicate that world-referenced and body-referenced signals come together in PPC neurons that respond specifically to conjunctions of the two types of input. Visual representations of objects and scenes in PPC thus contain spatial information that can be used in accurately guiding specific actions, such as targeting and grasping. Such a multiplicative mechanism is exactly what is needed to translate the allocentric entorhinal representation into goal-directed movements.

span.label: PPC neurons multiply world-referenced by body-referenced signals, which is what a coordinate transformation requires
span.quote: Such a multiplicative mechanism is exactly what is needed to translate the allocentric entorhinal representation into goal-directed movements.

span.label: grid cells are argued to rest on path integration because a periodic firing pattern persists through constantly changing speed and direction
span.quote: The expression of a strongly periodic spatial firing pattern in the presence of constantly changing running speed and running direction suggests that the grid must rely on path integration computations ( 16 , 19 , 20 ), where changes in velocity and direction are integrated over time to allow a constant representation of space

span.label: grids keep their relative geometry across environments, unlike place fields which remap
span.quote: Unlike place cells in the hippocampus, grid cells are activated in a stereotypic manner across environments, irrespective of the particular landmarks of the environment. Two cells in different parts of MEC whose grid fields are shifted and rotated 30° relative to each other in one environment will show the same relative shift and rotation in a different environment.

span.label: path integration drifts without recalibration against landmarks, which is why both mechanisms are needed
span.quote: Conversely, path integration can be used to build a metric representation of the animal's position in the environment, but without regular calibration against perceived or recalled landmarks and geometric boundaries, errors will accumulate and the representation will drift.

span.label: self-motion generates the firing but external cues anchor where it occurs
span.quote: The continued firing of place cells and grid cells in the absence of environmental cues does not mean they are not normally anchored to extrinsic inputs. Spatial representations in both the hippocampus and MEC rotate in accordance with the displacement of distal visual cues ( 6 , 7 , 16 ), firing fields in both regions can be transformed by extending or contracting the geometric boundaries of the recording enclosure ( 23 , 24 ), and self-motion-driven firing patterns in the hippocampus can be overridden by input from external landmarks ( 22 , 25 ). These observations demonstrate that, although the discharge patterns of place cells and grid cells may be generated primarily by self-motion, the locations of firing must be influenced to a great extent by external sensory cues.

span.label: PPC delay activity tracks the movement to be made rather than the target location, switching when the required effector changes
span.quote: These data, along with others, have led to the idea that cells in the PPC form a distributed representation of movement plans or intentions to make movements to specific goal locations

span.label: Whether PPC deficits actually reflect a failure to transform self-location into locomotor action is not established by the existing evidence.
span.quote: Whether they do remains open; at present, the evidence is ambiguous.

span.label: The direct medial entorhinal projection to PPC is weak and may not carry usable location information.
span.quote: This connection is relatively weak, and it is uncertain whether it is able to convey location information to possible action-preparing systems in PPC.

span.label: It is unknown whether medial entorhinal output actually targets the PPC neurons involved in action preparation.
span.quote: In principle, position can be reconstructed from the spike patterns of a very low number of grid cells ( 15 , 17 ), but it has not been determined whether the medial entorhinal outputs target those PPC neurons that are involved in action preparation.

span.label: Which of the candidate hippocampal-entorhinal to PPC routes actually carries the signal is unresolved.
span.quote: The relative contributions of the various pathways remain uncertain.

span.label: The whole account is at an early stage.
span.quote: We are just beginning to scratch the surface of this multitude of navigational control pathways.

span.label: in most lesion studies navigation impairments cannot be separated from memory impairments
span.quote: In the majority of these studies, the impairments in navigation can unfortunately not be distinguished from effects on memory.

span.label: the exact anatomical definition of rodent PPC remains a subject of debate
span.quote: Although an exact anatomical definition for the PPC in rodents remains a subject of debate (Box 1, Fig. 3 ), most lesion studies have focused on an area extending ≈2–6 mm posterior to bregma and 2–5 mm lateral to the midline, which includes most of the posterior neocortical area described as PPC.

span.label: whether to include parts of Oc2 is still controversial
span.quote: Whether or not to include parts of Oc2 in the PPC (i.e., the lateromedial extent of the PPC, or area 7) is still controversial.

span.label: head restraint in the primate work prevents any analysis of PPC during free locomotion
span.quote: While the functions described are likely indispensible to efficient spatial navigation, movement restrictions inherent to the head-restrained system prevent an analysis of the specific contributions made by the PPC during free locomotion.

span.label: a study contradicting the hippocampal path-integration account is set aside on the grounds that a dragged food cup may have left odour trails
span.quote: With the uncertainty about the availability of odor trails in mind, we suggest that the study is not decisive in negating the hypothesis that the hippocampus is essential to complex path integration in the rat (but see note added in proof).

span.label: the multiplicative gain-field mechanism for coordinate transformation, imported as the account of how a rodent map becomes motor output
span.quote: Such a multiplicative mechanism is exactly what is needed to translate the allocentric entorhinal representation into goal-directed movements.

span.label: the dorsal and ventral stream distinction and the deficits of parietal patients, used to motivate PPC's spatial role
span.quote: The dorsal stream, which provides the PPC with its visual input, has been described as being critical for spatial perception, enabling the representation of the locations of objects in space

span.label: parietal cortex is defined in the first line of the definition box by an overlying BONE, then immediately refined by cytoarchitecture, myeloarchitecture, neurochemistry and connectivity
span.quote: The parietal cortex is that part of the cortex that is covered by the parietal bone.

span.label: PPC is delimited by what it is between and by which thalamic inputs it lacks - a definition by exclusion and by neighbours rather than by intrinsic property
span.quote: This combination of thalamic inputs thus provides useful borders between PPC, somatosensory cortex, and visual cortex, respectively. These borders coincide with both cyto- and myeloarchitectonic criteria ( 76 , 100 , 108 ), as well as with changes in a number of other histochemical markers

span.label: place cells remap between environments while grid cells keep their relative geometry - the distinction that makes one a map of a place and the other a metric
span.quote: Unlike place cells in the hippocampus, grid cells are activated in a stereotypic manner across environments, irrespective of the particular landmarks of the environment. Two cells in different parts of MEC whose grid fields are shifted and rotated 30° relative to each other in one environment will show the same relative shift and rotation in a different environment.

span.label: the primate PPC literature shifted from a general spatial framework to multiple action-specific representations, so PPC function means something different before and after that shift
span.quote: More recently however, the emphasis in work on the PPC in primates has shifted away from the idea that it constructs an all-purpose framework for locating objects in space toward the notion that there are multiple spatial representations, each specialized to support a different action, such as eye movements, head movements, or grasping

span.label: extends → previous models in which parietal cortex mediates translation between external and first-person spatial representations (ref. 32)
span.quote: We propose here that this translation involves a transformation of output from the MEC circuit into body-based coordinates in parietal cortex, and that this transformation, aided by strong connections from parietal cortex to motor and premotor cortex ( 33 , 34 ), is necessary for guiding locomotor output during goal-oriented navigation.

span.label: builds-on → O'Keefe and Dostrovsky (1971) (ref. 4)
span.quote: Our understanding of the neural representation of navigational space began with the discovery of “place cells” by O'Keefe and Dostrovsky in 1971 ( 4 ).

span.label: contradicts → the study reporting that rats with partial hippocampal lesions returned to the start position (ref. 30)
span.quote: With the uncertainty about the availability of odor trails in mind, we suggest that the study is not decisive in negating the hypothesis that the hippocampus is essential to complex path integration in the rat (but see note added in proof).

span.label: extends → models proposing that parietal cortex translates between external and first-person spatial representations
span.quote: We propose here that this translation involves a transformation of output from the MEC circuit into body-based coordinates in parietal cortex, and that this transformation, aided by strong connections from parietal cortex to motor and premotor cortex ( 33 , 34 ), is necessary for guiding locomotor output during goal-oriented navigation.

span.label: qualifies → the study reporting intact path integration after partial hippocampal lesions
span.quote: With the uncertainty about the availability of odor trails in mind, we suggest that the study is not decisive in negating the hypothesis that the hippocampus is essential to complex path integration in the rat (but see note added in proof).

span.label: supports → the cognitive map account of hippocampal place cells
span.quote: Following these observations, it was proposed that the concerted activity of place cells provides the physiological substrate for a “cognitive map,” where cell populations throughout the hippocampus maintain a coherent, up-to-date representation of allocentric space and the animal's location in that space at any point in time

span.label: supports → the intention account of primate PPC delay activity
span.quote: These data, along with others, have led to the idea that cells in the PPC form a distributed representation of movement plans or intentions to make movements to specific goal locations

span.label: grid cells —operationalised-as→ path integration
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — inferential: the periodicity through changing speed and direction is the argument that path integration underlies the grid
span.quote: The expression of a strongly periodic spatial firing pattern in the presence of constantly changing running speed and running direction suggests that the grid must rely on path integration computations ( 16 , 19 , 20 ), where changes in velocity and direction are integrated over time to allow a constant representation of space

span.label: grid cells —distinct-from→ place cells
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS DEPENDENCE ON THE PARTICULAR ENVIRONMENT. 'UNLIKE PLACE CELLS IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS, GRID CELLS ARE ACTIVATED IN A STEREOTYPIC MANNER ACROSS ENVIRONMENTS, IRRESPECTIVE OF THE PARTICULAR LANDMARKS OF THE ENVIRONMENT.' Both are spatially tuned; only one re-maps, so a result obtained in a single environment cannot distinguish them at all - the distinction exists only across environments. Q-484. · strength of the relation: 1 — grids keep relative geometry across environments; place fields do not
span.quote: Unlike place cells in the hippocampus, grid cells are activated in a stereotypic manner across environments, irrespective of the particular landmarks of the environment. Two cells in different parts of MEC whose grid fields are shifted and rotated 30° relative to each other in one environment will show the same relative shift and rotation in a different environment.

span.label: allocentric —contrasted-with→ body-based coordinates
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the transformation between them is the paper's whole subject
span.quote: To traverse the environment, animals must be able to translate coordinate information from spatial maps in the entorhinal cortex and hippocampus into body-centered representations that can be used to direct locomotion. How this is done remains an enigma.

span.label: PPC —distinct-from→ somatosensory cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — distinguished by which thalamic inputs it LACKS, plus callosal connections - definition by exclusion
span.quote: This combination of thalamic inputs thus provides useful borders between PPC, somatosensory cortex, and visual cortex, respectively. These borders coincide with both cyto- and myeloarchitectonic criteria ( 76 , 100 , 108 ), as well as with changes in a number of other histochemical markers

span.label: path integration —contrasted-with→ cognitive map
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — complementary: one drifts without the other, which is why both are needed
span.quote: Conversely, path integration can be used to build a metric representation of the animal's position in the environment, but without regular calibration against perceived or recalled landmarks and geometric boundaries, errors will accumulate and the representation will drift.

span.label: The paper's central claim is that the posterior parietal cortex converts the world-centred position signal carried by place cells and grid cells into the body-centred coordinates that locomotion requires.
span.quote: We hypothesize that the essential contribution of the PPC is the translation of the animal's position from a world-centered coordinate system generated by place cells and grid cells into the body-based coordinates of locomotor actions.

span.label: Rats with PPC lesions cannot use their outbound self-motion to return to a refuge on a curtained circular arena, so the PPC deficit is not confined to vision.
span.quote: For example, when such animals leave a refuge to search for a randomly located food reward on a circular arena surrounded by a curtain, they are not able to return directly to the refuge based on their outbound movements

span.label: Rat PPC cells fire for conjunctions of a particular movement with a particular place - for instance only during outward forward running, or only during left turns at the end of an arm.
span.quote: For example, a PPC cell would fire during forward motion, but only when the animal was running outward from the center of the maze, whereas another cell would fire exclusively during left turns executed at the end of a maze arm

span.label: PPC firing fields rescale with the size of a maze segment even when hippocampal place fields do not, a dissociation implying PPC does not code perceived space.
span.quote: but the scaling occurred even under conditions where the size of hippocampal place fields remained constant. This dissociation suggests that PPC neurons do not express perceived space.

span.label: Anatomically there is no direct hippocampal or subicular input to PPC; the only direct route is a weak projection from the dorsal lateral band of medial entorhinal cortex.
span.quote: There are no direct connections to PPC from the dentate gyrus, hippocampus, or subiculum, but the dorsal part of the lateral band of the MEC, adjacent to the postrhinal cortex, has a direct PPC projection

span.label: Retrosplenial cortex damage, unlike postrhinal or prefrontal damage, produces lasting water-maze and path-integration deficits, making it a strong candidate relay from entorhinal cortex to PPC.
span.quote: damage to the retrosplenial cortex causes strong and lasting disruption of spatial navigation, both in the water maze ( 81 , 91 – 93 ) and in a path-integration task testing the ability to return directly to a home base in darkness

span.label: the entorhinal-hippocampal circuit alone cannot convert spatial information into goal-oriented motor output
span.quote: However, the entorhinal-hippocampal circuit alone cannot be sufficient for implementing the full array of computations necessary for spatial behavior. In addition to possessing a universal map of space, animals must also be able to convert the spatial information into goal-oriented motor output.

span.label: PPC neurons combine world-referenced and body-referenced signals multiplicatively
span.quote: Such a multiplicative mechanism is exactly what is needed to translate the allocentric entorhinal representation into goal-directed movements.

span.label: PPC delay activity follows the movement to be made, switching when the required effector changes
span.quote: These data, along with others, have led to the idea that cells in the PPC form a distributed representation of movement plans or intentions to make movements to specific goal locations

span.label: 77% of neurons in a medial PPC region responded to conjunctions of movement and location during virtual navigation
span.quote: In one such study, 77% of neurons recorded from a medial region of PPC responded to conjunctions of specific movements and specific locations during virtual navigation ( 52 ). In another study, approximately one quarter of the PPC cells were spatially tuned to path direction in a computerized maze task

span.label: grid fields keep their relative shift and rotation across environments, unlike place fields
span.quote: Unlike place cells in the hippocampus, grid cells are activated in a stereotypic manner across environments, irrespective of the particular landmarks of the environment. Two cells in different parts of MEC whose grid fields are shifted and rotated 30° relative to each other in one environment will show the same relative shift and rotation in a different environment.

span.label: place and grid firing persists without external cues but is anchored by them
span.quote: The continued firing of place cells and grid cells in the absence of environmental cues does not mean they are not normally anchored to extrinsic inputs. Spatial representations in both the hippocampus and MEC rotate in accordance with the displacement of distal visual cues ( 6 , 7 , 16 ), firing fields in both regions can be transformed by extending or contracting the geometric boundaries of the recording enclosure ( 23 , 24 ), and self-motion-driven firing patterns in the hippocampus can be overridden by input from external landmarks ( 22 , 25 ). These observations demonstrate that, although the discharge patterns of place cells and grid cells may be generated primarily by self-motion, the locations of firing must be influenced to a great extent by external sensory cues.

span.label: lesions of hippocampus, entorhinal cortex or PPC all disrupt return to a start location
span.quote: The conclusions from these studies are somewhat contradicted by a study in which rats with partial hippocampal lesions did return to the start position ( 30 ). The authors suggested that the hippocampal part of the circuit is not necessary for path integration.

span.label: place cell / place field
span.quote: these authors found that the firing of putative pyramidal cells in the dorsal hippocampus exhibited a striking behavioral modulation, where cells fired only when animals occupied particular locations, or “place fields,” in the recording environment

span.label: grid cell
span.quote: The multiple firing fields of cells in this region of entorhinal cortex formed a strikingly regular grid-like pattern composed of equilateral triangles tessellating the entire environment covered by the animal

span.label: cognitive map
span.quote: it was proposed that the concerted activity of place cells provides the physiological substrate for a “cognitive map,” where cell populations throughout the hippocampus maintain a coherent, up-to-date representation of allocentric space and the animal's location in that space at any point in time

span.label: posterior parietal cortex (PPC)
span.quote: Parietal cortex is typically divided into two regions, an anterior region with primarily somatosensory functions and a more complex multisensory posterior region, the posterior parietal cortex (PPC)

span.label: path integration
span.quote: where changes in velocity and direction are integrated over time to allow a constant representation of space

span.label: parietal cortex, by the overlying bone
span.term: parietal cortex, by the overlying bone
span.quote: The parietal cortex is that part of the cortex that is covered by the parietal bone.

span.label: PPC, by the combination of criteria
span.term: PPC, by the combination of criteria
span.quote: The definition of this area is commonly based on a number of criteria, such as topological relationships among cortical areas, as well as cytoarchitecture, myeloarchitecture, and expression patterns of different neuroactive substances and neurotransmitters. Combined with connectional criteria focusing on thalamocortical and/or corticocortical connectivity and functional (electrophysiological and behavioral) comparisons, it is apparent that a PPC can be defined in most if not all species.

span.label: place field
span.quote: By using microelectrodes chronically implanted in freely behaving rats, these authors found that the firing of putative pyramidal cells in the dorsal hippocampus exhibited a striking behavioral modulation, where cells fired only when animals occupied particular locations, or “place fields,” in the recording environment ( Fig. 1 A ). Outside of these fields, the cells were mostly silent.

span.label: grid
span.quote: The multiple firing fields of cells in this region of entorhinal cortex formed a strikingly regular grid-like pattern composed of equilateral triangles tessellating the entire environment covered by the animal

span.label: 77% — proportion of medial-PPC neurons in monkeys responding to conjunctions of specific movements with specific locations during virtual navigation
span.quote: In one such study, 77% of neurons recorded from a medial region of PPC responded to conjunctions of specific movements and specific locations during virtual navigation

span.label: ≈2–6 mm posterior to bregma and 2–5 mm lateral — stereotaxic extent of the rat cortical area targeted in most PPC lesion studies
span.quote: most lesion studies have focused on an area extending ≈2–6 mm posterior to bregma and 2–5 mm lateral to the midline

span.label: about 2 to 6 mm posterior to bregma and 2 to 5 mm lateral — where most rat PPC lesion studies have focused - compare Bucci2009, which gives 3.5 to 5.0 posterior and 1.0 or 1.5 to 5.0 lateral for the same region
span.quote: Although an exact anatomical definition for the PPC in rodents remains a subject of debate (Box 1, Fig. 3 ), most lesion studies have focused on an area extending ≈2–6 mm posterior to bregma and 2–5 mm lateral to the midline, which includes most of the posterior neocortical area described as PPC.

span.label: four published delineations, in red, yellow, magenta and blue — the number of incompatible published boundaries for rat parietal cortex, drawn on one brain in Figure 3
span.quote: Dorsal view of the right hemisphere of the rat brain showing the different delineations of the parietal cortex of the rat as reported by Krieg ( 100 ), in red; Palomero-Gallagher and Zilles ( 108 ), in yellow; Miller and Vogt ( 109 ), in magenta; and Burwell and Amaral ( 67 ), in blue.

span.label: 77% — neurons responding to movement-location conjunctions in virtual navigation
span.quote: In one such study, 77% of neurons recorded from a medial region of PPC responded to conjunctions of specific movements and specific locations during virtual navigation ( 52 ). In another study, approximately one quarter of the PPC cells were spatially tuned to path direction in a computerized maze task

span.label: four areas 7a, b, m and ip — the macaque subdivision whose applicability to rat is disputed
span.quote: Notwithstanding the overall agreement that PPC is present in the rat, the definition of this area still generates some controversy about how to specifically delineate it and whether it can be subdivided in the same way as in the macaque monkey, where four areas—7a, b, m, and ip—are distinguished ( 99 , 108 , 113 ). It is likely that a more systematic study of the connectivity pattern, including the connections with the thalamus, will eventually enable us to clearly define the PPC of the rat.

span.label: spacing, orientation and phase of the grid
span.term: spacing, orientation and phase of the grid
span.quote: All grid fields display the same iterative triangular geometry, but they may differ in spacing (distance between fields), orientation (the angle to which the maps are tilted), and phase ( xy offset of the fields relative to an external reference).

span.label: initial heading error in the water maze
span.term: initial heading error in the water maze
span.quote: As in the primate literature, deficits after lesions in PPC have traditionally been interpreted as perceptual impairments, reflecting a proposed role for this brain area in forming a spatial image based on visual and somatosensory inputs.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0804216105.
